newsitem.title: DUBAI: DUBAI INVESTMENT CO PLANS INDUSTRIAL PARK.
newsitem.headline: DUBAI INVESTMENT CO PLANS INDUSTRIAL PARK.

text.p: Dubai Investment Co (DIC), a leading share on the informal United Arab Emirates stock exchange, on Tuesday said it planned to build a private industrial park.
"International consultants are in the final stages of putting together a master plan for the Middle East's first industrial park," DIC's chairman Anis al-Jallaf told a news conference in Dubai.
The proposed industrial site, covering 30 square kms, would be located near the Jebel Ali free zone in Dubai, UAE.
"The industrial park will not be a free zone but it will offer other incentives that could attract local and international industries," he said.
Al-Jallaf said that DIC would also provide funding and management to attract companies to set up in the proposed park.
"If they have feasible projects we will go to the extent of funding, management and marketing," he added.
DIC has an authorised capital of 1.3 billion dirhams ($354 million) and paid up capital of 650,000 dirhams.
Dubai's government and local banks hold 45 percent of the equity in DIC and the remaining equity was offered for public subscription.
Distribution and blending of petroleum products are also on the company's agenda for 1997.
"We will go downstream all the way," said Khalid bin Kalban DIC's general manager.

"We are in the final stages of negotiations with an international firm to operate a blending and mixing unit to produce aromatics, plastics and other petroleum products," he said without disclosing the foreign partner's name.
Al-Jallaf said foodstuffs, distribution chains, hospital supermarket management, transportation and pharmaceuticals are also among DIC's priorities for 1997.
DIC said it had recently acquired stakes in a Dubai dairy factory, a glass factory and a building systems company worth some 170 million dirhams.

Earlier this year it bought a five percent equity share in the Al-Thuraya satellite system company, a $25 million project by UAE's communications giant Etisalat to operate a $1 billion mobile communications system. It had also acquired a 33 percent share in $12.5 million joint venture project with an Indian company to produce optic fibres.
